# Foundation current gap audit (2026-10-08)

## Current selector inventory

The 2026-10-10 `tools/binrecon/selector_check.py` rerun against the current
source and both reference images reports exact PPC selector coverage: 3,397
reference selectors and 3,397 source definitions, with no differences. i386
reports 3,253 reference selectors and 3,283 source definitions; its 30 extra
definitions are the PPC-only `NSURL` and `NSURLHandle` APIs retained as i386
stubs. Both targets report no missing, renamed, or duplicate selectors. This
inventory covers selector names only; it does not establish method-body or
ABI parity.

## `NSFileManager` account helpers

The current `NSFileManager.m` contains `_NSUserAccount` and `_NSGroupAccount`,
their lookup dictionaries and integer maps, passwd/group database scans,
entry initializers, dictionary accessors, equality/hash methods, and
`+[NSFileManager initialize]`. Their private ivar layouts match the records in
`reconstruction/abi/NSFileManager.json`. The group loader deliberately retains
the IDA-confirmed `NSNumber numberWithShort:` lookup against the integer-keyed
map; replacing it with a numeric pointer key would repair the reference's
observed behavior.

## `NSTimer` equality dispatch

The i386 bodies at `0x42583aa4` and `0x425306fc`, and PPC bodies at
`0x425998b0` and `0x4254075c`, confirm the source behavior. Base
`-[NSTimer _isEqualTimerWithTarget:selector:withObject:]` returns `NO` on both
targets. `NSConcreteTimer` requires the user-info-is-argument flag and matching
selector, then accepts pointer identity or `isEqual:` for both target and
user-info. No code change is needed.

## PPC fast Java bundle setup

Re-decompiled `_NSFastJavaBundleSetup` (`0x4257dd78`),
`_NSJavaPathCompsForBundle` (`0x4257ea94`), and the flag-controlled
`NSJavaBundleSetup` entry (`0x4257bb14`) from the current PPC IDA database.
`NSJavaSetup.m` matches the early VM reuse path, notification order, VM and
bundle path ordering, single fast-path library registration, system class
loader creation, loaded-state updates, requested-class loading, and return
paths. No source change was indicated.

## `NSJavaAbsolutePath` root predicate target split (2026-10-09)

Compared `_NSJavaAbsolutePath` in i386 (`0x425550ec`) and PPC
(`0x4257e684`). i386 sets its root-prefix flag from `!isEqualToString:@"/"`;
PPC sets it from `[root length] != 0`. Both reuse that flag when deciding
whether to prefix relative class paths. The source used the i386 predicate for
both targets, so PPC handled `"/"` and the empty string differently from its
binary. Split the predicate by architecture and renamed the local flag to
`useRoot`. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## Remaining implementation boundary

The normalized multiword `_NSIntegerDivide` algorithm was the known source
divergence in `NSDecimal.m`; following approval, it has now been reconstructed
from both target bodies. At the time of this inventory, nine PPC data exports
lacked proven reconstructed owners and widths. Later ABI ownership work
assigns `__NSMsgSendCount` to `NSPortMessage.m` and gives the eight compatibility
exports synthetic source definitions in `NSObjCRuntime.m`, recorded in the
source ownership and ABI manifests. Their original translation-unit provenance
and exact storage widths remain unknown.

Static source, IDA, and selector-inventory checks only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSUnarchiver decodeObject` reconstruction parity (2026-10-10)

Compared `-[NSUnarchiver decodeObject]` and its private `_decodeObject`
helper in i386 (`0x4250e4fc`, `0x42508a64`) and PPC
(`0x42508dcc`, `0x42502770`) with `NSArchiver.m`. Both decode reused `@`
descriptors for version 4 streams, return existing pointer-table objects
directly, and decode new instances through class resolution. Concrete data
classes use `decodeDataObject`; other classes are allocated in the object
zone and inserted before `initWithCoder:` to support cyclic references, then
passed through `awakeAfterUsingCoder:` and reinserted. Non-nil objects are
tracked in the growing unarchived-object array, and the object terminator is
validated. PPC's helper reads fields directly from the unarchiver; the source
copies the same fields into a stack context while preserving the mutable
cursor and label pointers. IDA compares the decoded class with the
`__NSConcreteDataClass` and `__NSConcreteMutableDataClass` globals. Source used
`NSClassFromString`, which also tries the alternate class-name mapping path;
it now uses the same globals, initialized by Foundation's process-start setup.
Both targets also send `isEqual:` to the selected true name with the archived
name immediately before class lookup; restored that message even though its
return value is unused.
The reused-string helper returns nil for the null marker in both targets, and
their `_decodeClass` bodies pass the result directly through length calculation
and NSString initialization. Removed the source-only missing-name exception to
preserve that call path. Static paired IDA/source review and whitespace check
only; no tests or builds were run.

## `_NSUTF8String` owner-array retain/release parity (2026-10-11)

Compared `_NSUTF8String` `allocWithZone:`, `init`, `dealloc`, `retain`,
`release`, `retainCount`, and `copyWithZone:` in i386 IDA (`0x42559bf0`,
`0x42562b20`, `0x42562adc`, `0x42514f60`, `0x42516f68`, `0x42562b68`,
`0x42528358`) and PPC IDA (`0x42562cc8`, `0x4256cefc`, `0x4256cea4`,
`0x425584e4`, `0x42558374`, `0x4256cf58`, `0x42558518`) with
`NSStringArray.m`. Both targets forward retain/copy and release to the owner
array count, saturate at `UINT_MAX`, record increment/decrement allocation
events at the same points, and deallocate the owner when release observes a
zero count. i386 guards count changes with `_NSGlobalRetainLock`; PPC uses
`__NSStringArrayRetainLock` only after `_NSIsMultiThreaded` becomes true. Source
preserves this lock split and ordering. Both targets reject direct abstract
allocation, initialization, and deallocation; source routes those operations
through `NSRequestConcreteImplementation`. No ownership or lock correction
indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

`+[NSMachPort portWithMachPort:]` (`0x42577594`, `0x42589c6c`),

`-[NSMachPort removeConnection:fromRunLoop:forMode:]` (`0x425345b4`,
`0x4252674c`) with `NSPort.m`. The factories preserve alloc/init/autorelease
order; the Mach-port factory returns nil for port zero. The allocator takes

review only; no tests or builds were run.

## Alternate class-name lookup implementation recheck (2026-10-12)

Compared `NSClassFromString` in i386 IDA (`0x42517610`) and PPC IDA
(`0x4250effc`), plus the `#` case in `_NSWalkData` in i386 (`0x4251db30`)
and PPC (`0x42509dac`), with `NSObjCRuntime.m` and `NSSerialization.m`.
Both `NSClassFromString` bodies call `cString`, then `objc_getClass`, and call

callback on a miss. Current source implements both paths; the pointer is
zero-initialized and assigned to `NSObjCRuntime.m` in the ABI, symbol, and
ownership maps. This confirms the earlier approval-pending gap is already
resolved in the current tree. Static paired IDA/source/metadata review only;
no tests or builds were run.

## `NSFileHandle` updating and writing path factories (2026-10-09)

Compared `fileHandleForUpdatingAtPath:` (i386 `0x42577068`, PPC
`0x4258960c`) and `fileHandleForWritingAtPath:` (i386 `0x425770b4`, PPC
`0x4258966c`) with `NSFileHandle.m`. Both targets allocate through `self` in
the null zone, initialize with the supplied path, then autorelease the result.
The updating factory passes `O_RDWR` (2) and create mode 0; the writing
factory passes `O_WRONLY` (1) and create mode 0. The concrete initializer in
i386 (`0x425798c0`) and PPC (`0x4258d304`) converts the path with a 1,024-byte
limit, opens through `_NSOpenFileDescriptor`, stores the descriptor on
success, and deallocates the receiver on conversion/open failure. Source
matches both factory call sequences and cleanup path. No source correction was
indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` formatter negative-result retry parity (2026-10-12)

Rechecked the scratch-buffer growth loop in `SubstituteFormat` in i386 IDA
(`0x42511bd8`) and PPC IDA (`0x42509ab0`) against `NSMutableString.m`. i386
repeats when `capacity <= vsnprintf(...)`; PPC repeats when
`_NSvsnprintf(...) >= capacity`. With the target's unsigned comparison, a
negative formatter result also triggers another growth attempt. Source
previously used a signed `count < capacity` success check, so `-1` incorrectly
fell through to `strlen` and replacement. The source now compares the result as
unsigned, preserving the target retry behavior on both architectures. Static
paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSMutableString` formatter conversion-class table parity (2026-10-12)

Decoded the 128-byte conversion-class tables used by
`-[NSConcreteMutableString setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:]` in i386
(`0x425a90eb`) and PPC (`0x425cf33c`). Both tables assign class 7 to the
format syntax characters `$`, `%`, `*`, and `.`, class 6 to `@`, class 3 to
`E`, `G`, `e`, `f`, and `g`, class 2 to `s`, class 4 to `p`, class 5 to `n`,
and class 1 to `X`, `c`, `d`, `i`, `o`, `u`, and `x`. These values match
the parser's conversion terminators, but the complete table comparison found
that source incorrectly assigned class 1 to unrecognized conversion
characters and class 7 only to `%`. Both targets' `IncrementArgPointer`
helpers advance by four bytes for class 1 and do not advance for class 0 or 7.
`NSStringFormatArgumentClass` now maps only the listed integer and character
conversions to class 1, maps all four syntax characters to class 7, and returns
class 0 for other characters. This corrects argument-cursor behavior for
unsupported and incomplete conversions; libc formatting output remains
outside this static comparison. Paired IDA table/helper/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteMutableCharacterSet initWithContentsOfFile:` PPC parity (2026-10-09)

Compared `-[NSConcreteMutableCharacterSet initWithContentsOfFile:]` in i386
(`0x425891d0`) and PPC (`0x4254ac44`) IDA with `NSCharacterSet.m`. Both targets
test `.bitmap` before `.dict`; bitmap files of length at most `0x1fff` retain
the `NSData` while borrowing its bytes, and longer files allocate `0x2000`
bytes and copy exactly that amount. Dictionary files load through
`dictionaryWithContentsOfFile:` and pass the result to the set parser. Missing
or unsupported files release the receiver and return nil. The source follows
these branch, ownership, and copy-length details. Static paired IDA/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSParser` initialization and teardown parity (2026-10-09)

Compared `-[NSParser initWithGrammar:]` (i386 `0x425313d4`, PPC
`0x425306c4`) and `-[NSParser dealloc]` (i386 `0x42531494`, PPC
`0x425308d4`) with `NSParser.m`. Both initializers obtain the zone from
`-[NSObject zone]`, copy the grammar into that zone, allocate and clear the
tokenization parameters, then install the default token rules without calling
`super init`. Source had an extra superclass initializer and nil return path;
it now follows the target sequence. Both deallocators free input and token
storage, release the grammar, release parse-stack objects from last to first,
free the stack and tokenization parameters, then release the parser's cached
strings before calling `super dealloc`. Source previously drained cached
strings first and freed the parse stack without releasing its objects. Updated
the lifecycle order to match both targets. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteMutableAttributedString initWithAttributedString:` (2026-10-08)

## `NSString writeToURL:atomically:` PPC conversion path (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x4258fec0`) and PPC (`0x425a7754`) IDA bodies with
`NSString.m`. i386 returns `NO` for non-file URLs and writes file URLs through
`writeToFile:atomically:`. PPC first sizes conversion with the default C
encoding, falls back to encoding 10 when needed, allocates a conversion buffer,
builds `NSData`, then forwards the URL write to that data. The source had only
the i386 file-URL path. Added the PPC-specific conversion and forwarding flow;
its selectors and arguments follow the PPC disassembly, including its lack of a
free for the temporary conversion buffer. Static paired IDA/source review and
whitespace checking only; no tests or builds were run.

Compared i386 (`0x4258fd74`) and PPC (`0x425a76f4`) with `NSString.m`. i386

## `_NSIsPList` accepted-type parity (2026-10-08)

The i386 `_NSIsPList` body (`0x42514670`) and PPC body (`0x42534cdc`) return
type 1 for `NSConstantString`, `NSInlineCString`, and `NSString` instances;
type 2 for `NSData`; type 3 for `NSArray`; and type 4 for `NSDictionary`.
For arrays and dictionaries, recursive validation checks each member with the
same accepted set. Neither target recognizes `NSNumber` or `NSDate`.
`NSUserDefaults.m` had included both classes in its type-1 branch; it now
accepts only the string family, matching these target categories. The serializers
(`0x42515744` i386 and `0x42546600` PPC) have no number or date encoding path
and fall through to the type-8 marker for unsupported values. Removed the
`NSNumber` and `NSDate` checks from `_NSIsPList`; the string, data, array,
dictionary, and recursive checks remain. Static source and whitespace checks
only; no tests or builds were run.

## NSDecimalNumber PPC retain-lock parity (2026-10-08)

The PPC `-[NSDecimalNumber retain]` (`0x4255e5b4`) and `release`
(`0x4255aeb8`) acquire a raw spin word only when `_NSIsMultiThreaded` is set,

IDA (`0x42549fc8`, `0x42553230`). Static paired IDA/source review and

Compared i386 (`0x42540fe0`) and PPC (`0x425472ac`) with
`NSStringEncodings.m`. After `getBytes:` succeeds, both targets raise
`NSCharacterConversionException` with
`"%@: didn't convert all characters"` when the remaining range is nonempty.
The source released the allocated data and returned nil instead. It now raises
using `_NSMethodExceptionProem(self, _cmd)`, matching both target paths.
Static paired IDA/source comparison and whitespace checks only; no tests or
builds were run.

For zero-capacity encodings, i386 returns the freshly allocated data object
without autoreleasing it, while PPC explicitly autoreleases before returning.
The source previously autoreleased in both cases; it now preserves this
ownership divergence with an architecture guard. This is visible for empty
strings converted to encodings whose capacity formula is zero. No ABI metadata
changed.

Also compared `removeTimersWithTarget:selector:withObject:` (i386
`0x42530138`, PPC `0x4253a864`) and `_invalidateTimers` (i386 `0x42549970`,
PPC `0x4253fe88`). Both targets reload `_timers` while iterating across timer
invalidation, then release the current vector. The source previously retained
the starting pointer across invalidation; it now follows the target reload and
release order. `containsTimer:forMode:` and `timersForMode:` matched the target
membership and default-mode behavior. Static paired IDA/source comparison and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

A follow-up confirmed the final-reference cleanup order: both `_invalidateTimers`
bodies release vector objects from the last slot to the first before freeing
the vector, while `NSRunLoopReleaseVector` releases from first to last. The
source now decrements the shared reference count directly and uses the target's
reverse release loop in this timer-specific path; other vector cleanup keeps
the shared helper. Static paired IDA/source comparison and `git diff --check`
only; no tests or builds were run.

`removeTimer:forMode:` (i386 `0x42581f14`, PPC `0x425977a8`) has one remaining
edge divergence: both targets clear the mode cache when the timer vector becomes
empty, then still read `fireDate` through the old first vector slot and set the
cache again. The source now keeps that sequence, matching the target's
post-removal slot read and cache update. This preserves the binary's observed
stale-slot lifetime hazard when the removed timer has no other owner. Static
paired IDA/source comparison only; no tests or builds were run.

releasing the initialized request; after a successful synchronous send, the
caller also has no explicit request release. `NSHTTPURLHandle.m` now preserves
that order and both ownership paths. Static PPC disassembly/source comparison
only; no tests or builds were run.

counts, and nil checks. Static PPC IDA/source comparison only; no tests or
builds were run.

## `NSPortMessage parseMachMessage:` out-of-line stream ownership (2026-10-08)

Compared i386 `0x4252cacc` and PPC `0x425218b8`. Both initialize the stream's
VM-data flag to zero. For inline byte/char descriptors with a stream, the
targets allocate ordinary zone storage and copy the bytes. For an
out-of-line descriptor with a stream, they adopt the descriptor pointer into
the stream and set its VM-data flag to one. Without a stream, they wrap an
out-of-line pointer in `NSData` using `copy:NO`, `freeWhenDone:YES`, and
`bytesAreVM:YES`. `NSPortCoder` uses the stream flag to select VM-page release
or zone free. The source now retains the inline copy path, adopts the
out-of-line pointer and sets `isVMData` for stream decoding, and wraps
out-of-line components with the VM-aware no-copy initializer. It clears the
local stream after the first byte/char descriptor, matching the target's
component-routing behavior. Static paired IDA/source review and whitespace
checks only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSPortMessage sendBeforeTime:` sender reconstruction gap (2026-10-08)

Rechecked i386 `0x4252ac14` and PPC `0x42520d90` against the current sender.
Both use a direct stream-buffer path only when `reserved != 0`, components are
nil, and the stream length is at most `0x2000`; this fills the 36-byte message
header and long-byte descriptor in the reserved prefix. Otherwise, they build
an 8-KiB local message, count only the supplied components, reserve 16 bytes
per component, enter the descriptor loop once and re-read the array count at
the loop tail, skip unsupported objects, and choose inline or out-of-line
byte descriptors based on remaining capacity. Port components mark the Mach
message non-simple. `NSPortMessage.m` now follows both packet paths, reserved
prefix behavior, component routing, timeout flags, and error results.

Both targets start send options at 33 (`SEND_TIMEOUT | SEND_SWITCH`), clear
the timeout bit for delays above `4294967.295` seconds, increment the exported
zero-initialized 32-bit `__NSMsgSendCount` immediately before `msg_send`, raise
`[NSPortMessage sendBeforeDate:] destination invalid` for `SEND_INVALID_PORT`,
return `NO` for `SEND_TIMED_OUT`, and raise
`[NSPortMessage sendBeforeDate:] Cannot send (%s)` for other errors. The
counter maps to the `DO` aggregate in both images. The reconstruction defines
the zero-initialized 32-bit counter in `NSPortMessage.m`, where the sender
increments it, and registers that source ownership; the original binary
translation unit remains unknown. Static paired IDA/source review and
whitespace checks only; no tests or builds were run.

## PPC data-export count reconciliation (2026-10-08)

The earlier “nine unassigned” inventory statements predate the
`__NSMsgSendCount` ABI ownership closure. Current reconstruction metadata
assigns that 32-bit export to `NSPortMessage.m`; its original binary input
translation unit is still unknown beyond the aggregate `DO.subproj_subproj.o`.
Eight PPC data exports remain without reconstructed source owners. Static
metadata/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

The current PPC export table identifies the eight as `_YES` (`0x425cbaa8`,
byte `01`), `_dummyPad1` (`0x425cbaac`, `00`), `_NO` (`0x425cbaaf`, `00`),
`_dummyPad2` (`0x425cbab0`, `00`), `_nil` (`0x425cbab4`, `00`), `_Nil`
(`0x425cbab8`, `00`), `___NSObjectAllocatorLock` (`0x42626254`, leading
bytes `00 00 00 00`), and `_NULL` (`0x42626360`, leading bytes `00 00 00 00`).
The i386 export table has the same byte values for `_YES` (`0x425a6374`),
`_dummyPad1` (`0x425a6375`), `_NO` (`0x425a6378`), `_dummyPad2`
(`0x425a6379`), `_nil` (`0x425a637c`), `_Nil` (`0x425a6380`), and `_NULL`
(`0x42602438`); it has no `___NSObjectAllocatorLock` export.
None has a source owner in `symbols.json` or `ownership.json`, and an exact
name search found no defining occurrence under `src/`. Their export bytes
alone do not establish which source translation unit or declaration owns
them, so they remain unmapped rather than being assigned speculatively. The
in-tree Objective-C runtime header defines `YES`, `NO`, `nil`, and `Nil` as
macros, while `objc-globaldata.m` contains no corresponding storage
definitions; that runtime source therefore does not explain these binary
exports either.

### PPC data-export reference check

The i386 and PPC `NSAllocateObject` wrappers (`0x42502d28` and
`0x42501814`) only select the default zone, call `_zoneAlloc`, optionally
record allocation statistics, and return the object. Neither wrapper accesses
the allocator-lock export. A current PPC IDA xref query reports no inbound
references to any of the eight exported data addresses listed above. Exact
source-name searches likewise find no definitions for these symbols under
`src/`; only unrelated uses of Mach `NULL` constants match `_NULL`. This does
not establish their owning translation units, so the exports remain unmapped
pending stronger ownership evidence. Static paired IDA/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle` interface-style resource suffix order (2026-10-08)

Compared i386 `___NSSearchBundleDirectory` (`0x4251d838`) and PPC
(`0x4250f3f4`) with the `NSBundleResourcePath` source helper. Both binaries
form the localized candidate by appending `-<NSInterfaceStyle>` to the resource
name before appending the extension. When the Windows-style fallback is enabled,
they similarly form `<name>-winnt.<extension>`. The current source first forms
`<name>.<extension>`, then appends `-<style>`; its Windows fallback appends
`-winnt` to that base path, which already includes the extension, and then
appends the extension again.
Thus style-specific resources such as `icon-windows.png` are missed and the
fallback candidate is malformed. The base resource check and the selection
order (base first, then style candidate, then Windows fallback) otherwise
match. This source snapshot described an open mismatch. The current-source
reconciliation at the end of this audit found the suffix order already fixed.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

A second predicate difference was found in that resource lookup helper. Both
`__NSIsResourceAtPath` bodies convert the candidate path, call `stat`, and
accept it when any owner/group/other read bit is present (`st_mode & 0x124`).
The source helper uses `fileExistsAtPath:` followed by `isReadableFileAtPath:`,
whose readability check calls `access(path, R_OK)`. These differ when the
process identity does not match the permission bit that is set (for example,
owner-only readable files viewed by another user, or mode-000 files read as
root). The source snapshot described this as a separate permission-predicate
mismatch. The current-source reconciliation at the end of this audit found the
target `st_mode & 0x124` predicate already present.

The candidate suffix loop also runs when `NSInterfaceStyle` is nil or empty:
`___NSSearchBundleDirectory` unconditionally writes `-`, copies the style's
zero characters, appends the extension, and tests that candidate after the base
resource exists. The source snapshot returned the base resource immediately
when style was nil or empty, so it skipped this `name-.ext` candidate. The
current-source reconciliation at the end of this audit found that candidate
already present. The Windows fallback is controlled separately by the
`windowsStyle` flag.

## `NSBundle findBundleResources:` zero-limit named lookup (2026-10-08)

Compared i386 `+[NSBundle findBundleResources:callingMethod:directory:languages:name:types:limit:]` (`0x42527820`) and PPC (`0x4251ef14`) with the source. For a non-null resource name, both binaries call `___NSSearchBundleDirectory` before checking whether the result count has reached `limit`; that helper adds a successful path without a limit argument. With `limit == 0`, a matching direct resource can therefore produce one result, after which the count check stops localized searches. The audited source snapshot returned an empty array immediately when `limit == 0`. Directory-listing paths check the limit in their loops. This was a confirmed named-lookup edge divergence in that snapshot; the current-source reconciliation at the end of this audit found the direct-candidate behavior already implemented.

For the `limit == 0` named path, the type loop also has a specific boundary:
with `types == nil`, the binary attempts the single extensionless candidate; with
an empty type array, it attempts none; with a nonempty array, it attempts only
the first type, then the `limit <= resultCount` check exits even if that
candidate misses. No localized language candidates are then searched. The
source snapshot's early zero-limit return missed each possible direct attempt;
the current-source reconciliation at the end of this audit found this boundary
already implemented.

### Allocation-failure path fidelity follow-up (2026-10-08)

The same i386 (`0x425366d8`) and PPC (`0x425b85bc`) parser bodies call `NSZoneMalloc` for the period array and abbreviation cache, then immediately zero each allocation with `memset`; they do not check either result or return a graceful failure on allocation failure. `NSTimeZone.m` now mirrors that call sequence, while retaining the allocation-size overflow preflight and malformed-record cleanup. This corrects the preceding source allocation-failure behavior description; no tests or builds were run.

### Parser output and abbreviation ownership parity (2026-10-08)

The i386 and PPC parser bodies leave both output pointers untouched on early validation failure, assign `*periods` immediately after allocating the period array, set `*count` only on success, and clear only `*periods` after a malformed-record failure. They create cached names with `stringWithCString:length:`, retain each name into its period, and free the pointer cache without releasing cached strings or period references on the malformed path. `NSTimeZone.m` now follows those output writes and ownership paths. This supersedes the earlier entry's statement that malformed-record cleanup remained unchanged. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## Correction: PPC `NSInvocation -invoke` return ownership (2026-10-08)

The 2026-10-07 dispatch summary incorrectly stated that PPC performs no return ownership work. Re-reading PPC `-[NSInvocation invoke]` at `0x4253d840` shows that after normal dispatch it calls `_NSParseAndRetain` for every non-void return and sets the retained-return flag. For object returns from `performSelector:` variants, it first asks the receiver for the invoked selector's signature; when present, a `v`/`V` return skips retention, while other encodings are parsed and retained. A missing signature falls back to the invocation's own signature. Updated `NSInvocationRetainReturnedValue` to match this PPC path while preserving the existing i386 return handling. The same lifecycle recheck confirmed that i386 reads the nested signature's `_types` field directly after `methodSignatureForSelector:`. The source used `methodReturnType`, which added an accessor dispatch absent from the target; it now reads the private layout field directly, matching both target paths. ## `NSConcretePortCoder decodeDataObject` inline-data path (2026-10-08)

Compared i386 `0x4253a710` and PPC `0x4253a184` with the source method. Both

`NSStreamData` object when the resulting pointer is four-byte aligned; when it

previously copied every inline payload through `dataWithBytes:length:`.

advancement. This is an inline-buffer
call-path mismatch: the aligned branch sends `subdataWithRange:` to the
embedded `NSStreamData`, with the range offset computed as the decoded pointer
minus `stream.start`. The paired `NSData -subdataWithRange:` bodies match
source: because the receiver is `NSStreamData`, a range longer than `0x7fff`
uses `NSSubrangeData`; shorter ranges copy only the selected bytes into
`NSData`. The unaligned branch also copies only the selected bytes through
`dataWithBytes:length:`. Thus the aligned large-range path also changes the
returned data class and backing-storage shape, beyond the call-path detail.
`decodeDataObject` now returns the `NSStreamData` subrange for aligned inline
payloads and preserves the copy path for unaligned payloads. Static paired
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcretePortCoder` typed-value walker integration (2026-10-08)

Both i386 (`encodeValueOfObjCType:at:` `0x42513800`,
`decodeValueOfObjCType:at:` `0x42519760`) and PPC (`0x4250d2d0`,
`0x425112e8`) are thin wrappers around `__NSWalkData`, passing the encode or
decode operation, pointer-walking enabled, the coder's stream, the value
address, and the type description. `NSPortCoder.m` instead special-cases
objects, sends integer scalars through the compact-integer helpers, and copies
all other values as raw bytes. That bypasses the target walker's recursive
handling of arrays, structs, pointers, qualifiers, and callback cases. The
source already contains `_NSWalkData`, but its generic archive callback table
uses uniform `(storage, value, width)` functions; the port coder's four-entry
table has distinct byte, fast-integer, C-string, and data signatures. In the
target, `_NSWalkData` receives the raw stream context: its cursor, limit,
function table, callback, and flag fields line up with the walker's context
offsets. However, the stream's first slot is `data`, initialized to NULL, and
the current generic walker passes `archive->storage` as the callback receiver;
stream mode must pass the stream context itself. The stream's `flags` field is
initialized to one, selecting the existing callback-based object encode/decode
path. `NSFastDecoderContext` also shares the stream's owner/cursor/limit prefix,
while offset calculation must use the stream's `start` field instead of
messaging `storage` for `bytes`. Stream-mode encoding must dispatch the table's
distinct callbacks by signature: the walker calls slot 0 for byte values,
slot 1 for compact integers, and slot 2 for C strings/selectors. Slot 3 is used
inside the C-string writer for the encoded payload, not as a direct walker
callback. The C-string callback takes the string value rather than the generic
table's pointer-to-value convention. Object values dispatch through the
callback field when the stream flag is set. Generic archive mode must retain
its current uniform callback table and storage receiver. A faithful correction
therefore needs this explicit stream mode (or an adapter preserving cursor
updates and callback flags) before the typed methods delegate. No source change
has been made. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were
run.

The live decompilations confirm the shared 32-bit context offsets directly:
i386 `_NSWalkData` is at `0x4251db30`, and PPC `_NSWalkData` is at
`0x42509dac`. The stream's `cursor`, `limit`, `start`, and function table are
the walker's fields 1–4; the coder callback is field 5, and the stream flag at
byte offset 24 selects callback-based object handling. Primitive byte, compact
integer, and C-string writes call function-table slots 0, 1, and 2 respectively.
This rules out using the stream's first `data` field as the generic storage
receiver: it is null in the initialized stream, while stream callbacks receive
the stream context itself. The context-mode dispatch must preserve those exact
receiver and signature differences on both targets.

### Typed walker short-integer callback distinction (2026-10-08)

The live i386 (`_NSWalkData` `0x4251db30`) and PPC (`0x42509dac`) bodies
confirm that `c`, `C`, `$`, `s`, and `S` values use the stream's byte-writer
callback. For `s` and `S`, each target invokes that callback twice, in
target-byte order. Four-byte (`i`, `I`, `l`, `L`, `f`) and eight-byte (`q`,
`Q`, `d`) scalar cases use the fast-integer callback with their full width.
`NSConcretePortCoder` now sends `c`/`C`/`$` through one byte callback and
`s`/`S` through two byte callbacks in `NSPortCoder.m`. It sends
`i`/`I`/`l`/`L`/`f` and `q`/`Q`/`d` through the fast-integer callback,
matching the target's four-byte and eight-byte scalar groups; this corrects
the previous raw-byte paths for `f` and `d`. Recursive arrays, structs,
pointers, and the other typed-walker cases remain part of the separate
integration gap above. Static paired IDA/source review and whitespace
checking only; no tests or builds were run.

### Typed walker pointer and object callback semantics (2026-10-08)

Both target `_NSWalkData` bodies use the pointer-walking flag to decide whether
to process `^` pointees. With pointer walking enabled, encode writes a
one-byte presence marker; a nonnull unqualified pointer recursively walks its
pointee type, while `O`/`R`-qualified object pointers require an `@` pointee
and recurse with the corresponding object qualifier. A null pointer writes a
zero marker. In stream mode, object values dispatch through the coder callback
field: encode calls `encodeObject:isBycopy:isByref:` with the active qualifier
flags, and decode calls `decodeRetainedObject`. These target paths confirm
that raw pointer or aggregate byte copies cannot preserve the recursive
object/ownership behavior. No source change was made. Static paired IDA review
only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSThread` bootstrap invocation ownership by architecture (2026-10-08)

invocation record in `reserved1` at offset 44, posts
`_NSThreadDidStartNotification`, invokes the target, then calls the instance
`_exit`; `dealloc` releases the record's target and argument and frees it.
`NSThread.m` now preserves these architecture-specific setup, notification,
exit, and ownership paths. Static paired IDA/source comparison and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSThread` thread-name call order (2026-10-08)

matches the target sequence. `_threadName` calls `cthread_name` twice on both

passes the first result and computes the length from the second. Source now
preserves both call count and order. Static paired IDA/source comparison and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSNumber -hash` floating-point finite range (2026-10-08)

Compared the floating-value branch of `-[NSNumber hash]` in i386

### `NSNumber -hash` NaN path

The floating-point branch's i386 unordered x87 comparison selects the signed
32-bit conversion path. PPC `fcmpu` marks unordered, then `cror SO,EQ,GT`
clears the branch bit, sending NaN through the negative conversion path.
Both targets' invalid integer conversions produce the `INT_MIN` sentinel, so
the existing source's explicit NaN return matches. No code change was
indicated. Static paired IDA/source review; no tests or builds were run.

## PPC `NSGetSizeAndAlignment` leading-double struct alignment (2026-10-09)

PPC `__NSGetSizeAndAlignment` (`0x4250bffc`) starts struct double alignment
at 4 and promotes it to 8 only when the first field encoding (after the target
field qualifiers) is `d`; all later double fields use that selected alignment.
i386 (`0x42522e80`) uses alignment 4 for every double field. Added this
PPC-only rule to the recursive struct layout, retaining the existing i386 path.
Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `NSGetSizeAndAlignment` union and bitfield layout parity (2026-10-09)

The i386 `_getBitfieldSizeAndAdvance` (`0x425767b4`) and PPC helper
(`0x425888c0`) both pack consecutive `bN` fields into 32-bit units, report
alignment 4, pad zero-width fields to a word boundary, and restart a field
when it exceeds the remaining bits in a word. Aggregate walkers pass the
current byte offset and add the helper's rounded byte count. Replaced the
source's independent `bN` byte count with the same run-based packing helper.

Both targets report union size as the maximum ordinary field size without a
final size round-up and omit bitfields from that maximum. The original PPC
review incorrectly concluded that `double` fields were omitted from the union
maximum. The 2026-10-12 instruction-level recheck below corrects that
conclusion: PPC includes each parsed non-bitfield size, including `double`,
while its alignment still follows the leading-double rule. The source also
accumulates offsets for union bitfield parsing. Direct `b` encodings use each
target's unknown-type result. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

match these exception and cursor paths. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

`st_mode` directly.

## `_NSDeserializeObject` collection reconstruction parity (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x42509a48`) and PPC (`0x4252f0ec`) with `NSSerialization.m`.
Both targets defer temporary pointer-array allocation until after the lazy
fault path, allocate/free those buffers with a null zone, and release retained
elements in reverse order. Array decoding compacts nil results by swapping in
the last element and logs the target's nil-array message. Dictionary keys are
decoded immutable and eagerly; pairs with a nil key or value are similarly
swapped out and logged. Source previously allocated before the lazy return,
preserved array/pair order while filtering, used mutable/lazy settings for
keys, and released in forward order. Lazy-fault completion also releases in
reverse order. The initial review interpreted the i386 dispatcher's incomplete
three-argument decompiler signature as evidence that nested values used
immutable/eager defaults, and guarded the saved flags to PPC. Follow-up i386
call-site disassembly showed that all six arguments are pushed and `_mutable`
and `_lazy` are forwarded for nested values; dictionary keys still use zero
flags. The source now uses the saved flags on both targets; see the 2026-10-11
nested-mutability entry below. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## PPC ABI and C-symbol coverage reconstruction (2026-10-09)

Regenerated the PPC class/category ABI records from the live Foundation
`__OBJC` module-info records. Reconciled the 12 changed snapshots and added
records for the nine missing Objective-C modules; added a symbols-only
`NSPortMessage` record for its source C-symbol ownership. The set now has 90
documents: all 85 Objective-C modules plus five source modules without a
module-info record. Rebuilt the PPC C-symbol assignments from the shared
source-to-module map, retaining only symbols that the PPC image defines as
external and preserving existing PPC-only external assignments. This covers
all 415 exported C text symbols and 307 of 315 exported C data symbols, with no
duplicate owners or section/binding mismatches. The eight exported data names
without a Foundation module owner are `_NO`, `_NULL`, `_Nil`, `_YES`,
`___NSObjectAllocatorLock`, `_dummyPad1`, `_dummyPad2`, and `_nil`; left these
unassigned pending ownership evidence. All 90 documents pass the ABI schema
check, their 3,397 method selector names match the PPC selector symbol set,
and the 415 C text assignments match the exported text-symbol set. Static
extraction and inventory checks only; no tests or builds were run.

Follow-up ownership tracing found no exact definitions for these eight names in
the Foundation source tree, and the PPC IDA database marks each symbol public
with no data cross-references. Six reside in `__TEXT,__const`; `___NSObjectAllocatorLock`
and `_NULL` reside in `__DATA,__data`. There is no evidence assigning them to a
Foundation source module, so they remain outside the per-module C-symbol lists
pending a source or link-map attribution.

a bitfield-aligned member. Updated the array stride calculation to match both

## `NSUnarchiver` C-string result ownership parity (2026-10-09)

Compared `_decodeValueOfObjCType` in PPC IDA (`0x42501904`) and recovered its
i386 `'*'` jump-table case from the dispatch at `0x42507bc0`. The i386 table
entry for descriptor index 9 targets `0x42507eac`. Both target bodies decode a
new or reused C string, register it in the pointer table, then copy each
nonnull result including its NUL terminator into `context->objectZone` before
returning it. In i386, the case calls `__decodeReusedCStringUsingTable`
(`0x425066dc`), inserts into the pointer table through `_objc_msgSend`
(`0x426006de`), and allocates through `j__NSZoneMalloc` (`0x4260012e`); PPC
shows the same sequence in its decompilation. `NSArchiver.m` had returned the
string-table pointer directly. The zone copy now applies on both targets,
after pointer-table registration, preserving table identity and the target
result lifetime. Static IDA/source review and diff checking only; no tests or
builds were run.

nonnull results, matching both targets. Static IDA/source review and diff

range. The Shift-JIS wrapper advances its input cursor by the converted byte
count on successful conversion. Source cursor updates match those successful
paths; the failed-conversion path has a separate uninitialized-local issue
documented in the current-source recheck below.
`NSNEXTSTEPToPrecompUnicode` also matches the ASCII-direct and
high-byte-table paths. No correction was indicated. Static paired IDA/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSShiftJISToUnicode` failed-conversion consumed-count recheck (2026-10-12)

Rechecked i386 (`0x4259203c`) and PPC (`0x425a97cc`) disassembly and
pseudocode against `NSShiftJISToUnicode` in `NSCharConversion.m`. Both targets
pass a stack local as `NSShiftJISToEUC`'s consumed-count output, then read it
without initializing it first. The helper's invalid-input returns do not
write that output. The caller therefore has undefined behavior for malformed
Shift-JIS input: it may treat the stale value as zero and consume one byte, or
use an arbitrary nonzero count. Current source initializes the count to zero,
so its failure path deterministically consumes one byte and returns failure.
Keep that defined source behavior; removing the initializer would introduce
undefined behavior without reproducing a stable target result. Successful
conversion paths remain matched. Static paired IDA disassembly/pseudocode and
source review only; no tests or builds were run.

(i386 `0x425282b4`, PPC `0x42531fb8`) with `NSPrivate.m`. Both targets use
500-byte chunks, return exact-size autoreleased chunks for larger requests, and

instance allocator advances its byte offset without bounds checks, and

conditions. No correction indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSDecimalCompare`, normalize, subtraction, and division parity (2026-10-09)

Compared `_NSDecimalCompare` (i386 `0x425a0930`, PPC `0x4255a580`),
`_NSDecimalNormalize` (i386 `0x425a0fb0`, PPC `0x4255edec`),
`_NSDecimalSubtract` (i386 `0x425a14c4`, PPC `0x425c4bfc`), and
`_NSDecimalDivide` (i386 `0x425a0a34`, PPC `0x425c44a0`) with `NSDecimal.m`.
Both comparison bodies check not-a-number and sign state before zero length,
copy and normalize operands, compare mantissas, then reverse non-equal results
for negative values. Normalization selects the operand with the larger exponent,
tries full power-of-ten alignment, and on precision loss reduces the alignment
using `NSIntegerMaxPowerOf10Multiplier`. Subtraction toggles the nonzero right
operand's sign and delegates to addition. Division handles not-a-number, zero
divisor, and zero dividend, computes the quotient after 38 decimal guard digits,
tracks discarded remainders, then sets sign/exponent and compacts. Source matches
both target paths; no correction indicated. Static paired IDA/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.

length and sign for zero operands, multiply mantissas, combine signs and
exponents, discard excess base-10 digits while tracking a possible tie, apply
the selected rounding mode, store the resulting mantissa and length, and
compact. The i386 rounding dispatch is a jump table; PPC expresses the same
rounding modes as branches. The shared source helpers implement the equivalent
rounding decision and discarded-digit adjustment. No source correction was
indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

reject NaN operands, copy through zero operands, normalize nonzero operands,

opposite-sign magnitudes while retaining the larger magnitude's sign. Both
preserve the normalization error unless addition's rounding reports loss of
precision, detect positive exponent overflow, clear the compact flag, and

branches; both implement the source `RoundToFit` policy. No target-specific

## `NSConcreteMutableString setStringWithFormat:` mutation-order gap (2026-10-09)

Compared `-[NSConcreteMutableString setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:]`

`NSMutableString.m`. Both targets get the receiver's length, replace its full
range with the format string, then get the format's length before parsing and
substituting directly into the receiver. Source also parses and substitutes
directly into the receiver, but it used to ask for the format length first and
read the receiver length from its ivar. It now uses `[self length]` before the
replacement and asks the format for its length afterward. Thus the earlier
recursion claim was incorrect; the current `NSString initWithFormat:locale:arguments:`
allocates a concrete mutable string and dispatches to this direct parser. A
focused comparison of `_SubstituteFormat` (i386 `0x42511bd8`, PPC
`0x42509ab0`) also found that both targets pass a nonnil object's description
result directly to the replacement call, even if that result is nil; source
previously converted a nil description result to `"(null)"`. The source now
preserves the target's direct result while retaining `"(null)"` for a nil
`%@` argument. A further return-value comparison found that both IDA targets
measure the mutable string's length before replacement and return the
replacement's effective character-count delta. `NSStringFormatSubstitute` in
`NSMutableString.m` instead returns `strlen` of the formatted C buffer for
non-object conversions. This can produce a different subsequent output offset
when decoding or locale replacement changes the character count.
`NSStringFormatSubstitute` now derives the inserted character count from the
receiver's length before and after replacement, adding back the replaced
format span. Positional width/precision stars also needed a correction:
both targets record the indexed star argument and its format offset, then
remove the `*n$` marker before substituting the integer width or precision.
The source records the index but `NSStringFormatResolveStars` replaces only
the `*`, leaving the `n$` suffix in the format passed to `vsnprintf`. This is
an additional mismatch in the same parser family; it now removes the matching
one-digit positional marker as it substitutes the value. Full conversion-by-
conversion parity remains unverified. Static paired IDA/source review and
whitespace checking only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteMutableString setStringWithFormat:` parser record pass (2026-10-09)

Further decompilation of i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`) shows the
shared high-level parser structure. Both clear the receiver first, fetch the
format as UTF-16 in chunks of at most 32 code units, scan until the `0xffff`
end sentinel, and collect each conversion in a 48-byte record. Literal code
units advance the output position. Conversion records retain the specifier,
argument class/index, width and precision star references, and output offset.
The first pass recognizes one-digit positional `$` references and classifies
positional versus sequential argument use. A second pass lays out positional
argument pointers using `_IncrementArgPointer`, resolves width/precision
arguments, then calls `SubstituteFormat` for each record and adjusts later
output offsets by the amount inserted.

`SubstituteFormat` formats numeric conversions into a scratch buffer starting
at 512 bytes and doubles it when the formatter reports insufficient capacity.
The architecture split is explicit in the helper bodies: i386 calls
`vsnprintf`, while PPC calls `_NSvsnprintf` (`0x425138d0`), preserving the
target's custom PPC formatter path. Both helpers insert the formatted bytes
directly into the receiver; `%@` takes the object-description path instead.
For `%@`, both targets use `descriptionWithLocale:` when supported, otherwise
`description`, and replace nil with the literal `(null)`. With a locale and
floating conversion, they look up the locale decimal separator and replace the
formatted period with its first character. `_IncrementArgPointer` advances
four bytes for argument classes 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6, and eight bytes for class 3
on both targets. Both `_SubstituteIntArgument` bodies consume an int from the
positional argument-pointer table, clamp negative width/precision to zero and
values above 999999999 to that maximum, format the integer into a ten-byte
temporary, then move the conversion-record tail over the temporary padding and
adjust its recorded length. The i386 pseudocode omitted the varargs value to
`__NSsnprintf`; i386 disassembly (`0x42593324`) confirms the load, clamp, and
pushed value. PPC disassembly (`0x425ab044`) confirms the same behavior. This
evidence refines the open formatter design; no source change was made. Static
paired IDA decompilation/disassembly only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteMutableString setStringWithFormat:` implementation (2026-10-09)

Implemented the approved direct parser in `NSMutableString.m`. The receiver is
seeded with the format string, scanned as UTF-16 chunks of at most 32 code
units, and conversion spans are retained in nine 48-byte records. Sequential
records format through i386 `vsnprintf` or PPC `_NSvsnprintf`; `%@` uses the
locale-aware description selector when available and `(null)` for nil.
Positional references use the IDA-confirmed one-digit argument table and
positional width/precision values are clamped to 0..999999999. Floating output
uses the first locale decimal-separator character. The IDA character-class map
assigns `%@` class 6, floating conversions class 3, `%s` class 2, `%p` class 4,
`%n` class 5, and integer/character conversions class 1; the argument cursor
advances eight bytes for class 3 and four for classes 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6.
In positional mode, an unindexed conversion uses slot zero, matching the
record's zero-initialized argument index. Static source review only; no tests
or builds were run.

Inspected the i386 `_argumentTypeSet.422` table at `0x425a90eb` and PPC `_argumentTypeSet.356` at `0x425cf33c`, used by `setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:` (`0x4250ab70` i386, `0x4250f9dc` PPC). Both tables agree: integer class 1 for `c d i o u x X`; double class 3 for `e E f g G`; class 2 for `s`, 4 for `p`, 5 for `n`, 6 for `@`, and 7 for parser syntax `$ % * .`. `NSStringFormatArgumentClass` recognizes the same conversions and assigns the same classes. `_IncrementArgPointer` (i386 `0x4250cc14`, PPC `0x4250a9bc`) advances classes 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 by four bytes, class 3 by eight, and leaves class 7 unchanged; `NSStringFormatAdvanceArgument` matches. `_SubstituteIntArgument` (i386 `0x42593324`, PPC `0x425ab044`) clamps star arguments to 0…999,999,999 before formatting; the i386 disassembly and PPC pseudocode confirm the source helper's same bounds. No source correction indicated for this slice. Scanner sequencing is documented in the paired bounds and substitution-order entries below. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` format scanner and positional-mode bounds (2026-10-10)

Compared the scanner in `setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:` in i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`) with `NSMutableString.m`. Both targets read UTF-16 input in chunks of at most 32 code units, retain at most nine positional conversion records, and cap each conversion token at 31 bytes including `%`; sequential conversions reuse one record and are substituted inline. Internal positional argument handling recognizes one-digit indexes 1–9. A positional value index selects positional mode only on the first conversion record; positional star indexes alone do not select it, and a later positional index does not switch a format already parsed in sequential mode. The source scanner and record handling match these limits and transitions. Together with the conversion-class audit above, source-to-target dispatch and argument-width handling are accounted for; exhaustive libc formatting results remain outside this static comparison. No source correction indicated. No tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` mixed sequential and positional format mode (2026-10-10)

The i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`) scanners enter positional mode only when a positional value index appears in the first conversion record. Once a sequential conversion has set the parser state to sequential, a later `%N$` token is normalized but does not switch argument selection to positional mode. `NSMutableString.m` previously set its global `positional` flag unconditionally during the second token pass, so a later positional conversion incorrectly reinterpreted earlier and later arguments. The source now switches modes there only for the first conversion record; its earlier detection already handles `%N$` while the first token is being scanned. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` sequential substitution order (2026-10-10)

Compared `setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:` in i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`). Both targets call `SubstituteFormat` immediately after parsing each sequential conversion, then advance the argument pointer for width, precision, and value arguments. They reuse one conversion record for this path; positional mode stores records for the deferred substitution pass. `NSMutableString.m` now substitutes each sequential token during scanning, adjusts subsequent source offsets for earlier replacements, and advances its local argument pointer afterward. The positional pass is covered by the paired audit below. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` sequential star argument advancement (2026-10-10)

The same i386 and PPC bodies track width and precision stars with separate Boolean fields, then advance the sequential argument pointer once per field. The source previously counted every `*` character, so repeated stars in one field advanced too many slots. It now tracks whether a width star and/or precision star occurred and uses those flags for cursor advancement. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

two entries only when the comparator is positive, and use the same three-item
comparison network. Recursive calls split at `count >> 1`; when boundary
checking is enabled, an already ordered pair of runs either returns the source
or copies both runs to the destination. The merge copies the left item first
when the comparator returns zero, preserving the target's stable ordering,
and then copies the remaining run with `memmove`. The i386 and PPC callers
(`sortUsingFunction:context:` at `0x4253c79c` and `0x42545848`) both use a
1536-byte stack buffer through 128 objects, allocate three object arrays above
that threshold, and enable boundary checks only above 63 objects. `NSArray.m`
matches these branches and thresholds. No source correction indicated. Static
paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## i386 `NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` positive-table boundary (2026-10-10)

Rechecked `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` in i386 IDA (`0x425a1d70`) against
`NSDecimal.m`. The positive path repeatedly subtracts 38, then passes each
intermediate row's count and following word address to `NSIntegerMultiply`.
The first intermediate for a requested power above 26,401 is row 26,364;
IDA shows that and the following rows through 26,422 carry count `0xffff`,
with no captured divisor payload. The source guard at 26,401 therefore stays
at the last fully retained positive divisor path. The count-only extension
through row 26,422 is used only by the negative path's compare-and-clear
handling, which does not read the unavailable words when their length exceeds
the dividend. Static IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` in-image caller power bounds (2026-10-10)

Both IDA databases have only two callers of `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10`:
`_NSDecimalDivide` and `_NSDecimalNormalize`. Division scales by 38.
Normalization derives its first power from the difference of two signed
8-bit exponents (absolute maximum 255); its fallback is bounded by the
eight-word `NSDecimal` capacity and that same difference. Therefore the
mapped-table gap above 26,401 on i386 and 26,806 on PPC is unreachable through
the reference's in-image callers. The helper remains an exported private
symbol, so arbitrary direct-call powers beyond the captured image data are
still an unverified edge; source retains its mathematical fallback there.
Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds
were run.

targets first handle tilde-only user completion by enumerating passwd names,
filtering on the typed prefix, collecting `~name` results in a set, and
returning the array plus its case-sensitive common prefix when requested. The
filesystem path handles trailing slash or backslash as an empty component
prefix; otherwise it splits the path into directory and last-component prefix.
Each search passes `filterTypes` to `_NSDirectoryContentsMatchingPrefixAndSuffixes`.
Multiple matches return their common prefix and full array. One match that is a
directory becomes the next search directory; a file or a directory with no
further matches returns that candidate and a one-element result array. Both
targets return zero when the initial search is empty and no candidate exists.
The source matches the branch order, output-pointer guards, and return counts;
no source correction was indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

receiver under `_NSString` in the exception user-info dictionary. The target

## `NSString` lossy ASCII converter branch parity (2026-10-10)

Rechecked `_NSUnicodeToLossyASCII` in i386 (`0x4259269c`) and PPC
(`0x425aa098`) IDA against `NSStringEncodings.m`. Both targets first try the
ASCII converter, then use a NEXTSTEP result only when its byte is at least
`0x80`; they index the 128-entry table by subtracting `0x80`. A failed
NEXTSTEP conversion advances the reader once before emitting `_`; a successful
low-byte conversion emits `_` without advancing again. Source previously
consulted an extra low-byte table on that latter path. Removed that unreachable
lookup and now preserve the target branch and reader behavior directly. The
high-byte table's 512-byte output map is identical in both target images and
matches all 128 packed source entries. Static paired IDA/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.

(`0x425664d8`) IDA with `NSSet.m`. Both targets return nil for an empty
simple dictionary, then scan buckets from the highest index downward and return
the first stored key. The source performs the same count check and descending
bucket traversal. No source correction indicated. Static paired IDA/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteSet anyObject` bucket-count dispatch parity (2026-10-10)

Compared `-[NSConcreteSet anyObject]` in i386 (`0x4255bbbc`) and PPC
(`0x4256579c`) IDA with `NSSet.m`. Both targets first reject a null table,
then obtain the bucket count and scan bucket indexes from high to low, returning
the first stored value. Neither calls `NSSimpleSetCount`; the mutable-set
override does call that helper on both targets. The immutable source had an
extra count call and early return, which could hide a populated bucket when
the table count is inconsistent. Removed that source-only check while
preserving the null-table guard and descending scan. Static paired
instruction/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSSimpleDictionaryDeleteEntriesWithValue` target parity (2026-10-10)

Compared `_NSSimpleDictionaryDeleteEntriesWithValue` in i386 (`0x42563400`)
and PPC (`0x4256da30`) IDA with `NSSimpleDictionaryDeleteEntriesWithValue`
and `NSSimpleDictionaryRemoveBucket` in `NSSimpleHashing.m`. Both targets
return early on an empty table, scan buckets from high to low, remove every
occupied entry whose value matches, compact dense tables at levels zero or one,
and otherwise leave tombstones. Both restore the table's count while preserving
its level. On empty input, i386 returns the existing table and PPC returns
null; the source preserves this split. The architecture-specific resize return
values and capacity checks also match. No source correction indicated. Static
paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSCountedSet` dictionary reference-count mutation path (2026-10-10)

Compared `-[NSCountedSet addObject:]` (i386 `0x4255c188`, PPC
`0x42566344`) and `removeObject:` (i386 `0x4255d12c`, PPC `0x425675e8`), plus
`_NSSimpleDictionaryIncrementValue` and `_NSSimpleDictionaryDecrementValue`,
with `NSSet.m` and `NSSimpleHashing.m`. Both targets reject nil before hashing.
Insertion increments an existing bucket value and returns its canonical key, or
sets a new bucket value to one, saturates the packed count field, and resizes
when the current capacity is exceeded. Removal skips hashing when the table is
empty, decrements the matching value, and releases the canonical stored key
only when the value reaches zero. The source preserves these branches and
ownership order; its lookup helper's empty-count check is reached only after
the caller's matching nonempty guard. Static paired IDA/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSCharConversion` byte-to-Unicode dispatcher parity (2026-10-10)

Compared `_NSConvertToASCIIorUnicode2` in i386 IDA (`0x42505944`) and PPC
IDA (`0x425044e8`) with `NSCharConversion.m`. For recognized encodings, both
binaries and the source follow the same dispatch: UTF-16 input recognizes and

Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSStringArray stringArrayWithBitVector:` selected-buffer capacity (2026-10-11)

Compared i386 (`0x4256270c`) and PPC (`0x4256ca4c`) with
`NSStringArray.m`. Both return nil for a zero-bit vector, lazily initialize
empty cached `_data`, scan its NUL-terminated entries while the bit index is
below the vector's bit count, append selected entries including their NUL, then
construct via `stringArrayWithUTF8Data:` and release the temporary buffer. On
the first selected entry, both targets initialize `NSMutableData` capacity to
the number of bytes remaining from the current entry to the end of `_data`:
i386 pushes `end - cursor`; PPC passes `end - cursor` in `r5`. Source previously
used a fixed capacity of 64. It now uses `(unsigned)(end - cursor)`, matching
both targets. Static paired IDA/source review and targeted `git diff --check`
only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSValue` range and rectangle return ABI parity (2026-10-11)

Compared `-[NSValue rangeValue]` and `rectValue` in i386 (`0x425a01e4`,
`0x425a0214`) and PPC (`0x425c3bf4`, `0x425c3c40`) IDA with `NSValue.m`.
Both methods call `getValue:` on the receiver, then return the copied aggregate.
On i386, `rangeValue` returns its two words in the integer return registers;
`rectValue` copies four words to the aggregate-return buffer. PPC receives the
return-buffer pointer separately, calls `getValue:` on the receiver, copies the
range or four rectangle words to that buffer, and returns its address. The
i386 decompiler labels the first stack argument to `rectValue` as `retstr`,
which makes the receiver look incorrect in pseudocode; the instruction sequence
and matching PPC body confirm the source's `[self getValue:&value]` path. No
source correction indicated. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly review
only; no tests or builds were run.

Both targets route `launchPath`, `arguments`, `environment`, `currentDirectoryPath`, and the three standard-handle getters, plus their seven setters, through `NSRequestConcreteImplementation` using the `NSTask` class. The source base methods make the same requests; `NSConcreteTask` supplies the concrete dictionary-backed accessors. No source correction indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteTask` copied-property setter call order (2026-10-11)

Rechecked `setLaunchPath:`, `setArguments:`, `setEnvironment:`, and
`setCurrentDirectoryPath:` in i386 IDA (`0x4257b97c`, `0x4257b73c`,
`0x4257b8bc`, `0x4257b7fc`) and PPC IDA (`0x4258f828`, `0x4258f5a0`,

Both targets check `_hasExeced`, lazily create and retain `_dictionary`, then
copy the supplied value, store it under the property key, and release the
temporary copy. `NSTaskSetCopiedObject` now follows this order. If copying
raises while `_dictionary` is nil, the initialized default task dictionary
remains retained, matching both target implementations. Static paired
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSString` zone-specific placeholder factory parity (2026-10-11)

Compared `_NSPlaceholderStringFromZone` in i386 IDA (`0x42503c08`) and PPC
IDA (`0x42503a3c`) with `NSString.m`. Both keep a cached placeholder for the
most recently requested zone, search the retained placeholder array in reverse
on a cache miss, allocate a placeholder with no extra bytes in zone `NULL`,
store the requested zone, add it to the array, and release the allocation's
initial retain. Both initialize the array with capacity 8 (the i386
disassembly confirms the immediate `8`, although its pseudocode omits it).
i386 conditionally locks the `NSLock` global; PPC acquires/releases the
spinlock only when `_NSIsMultiThreaded` is set. Source preserves this target
split and both cache paths. No correction indicated. Static paired
IDA/pseudocode/disassembly and source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSNumber copyWithZone:` buffer, conversion, and cleanup parity (2026-10-11)

Compared `-[NSNumber copyWithZone:]` in i386 IDA (`0x4259d3b0`) and PPC
IDA (`0x425c0ec8`) with `NSValue.m`, plus their shared `_newNumber`
conversion helper in i386 (`0x42554518`) and PPC (`0x425c7794`). Both copy
the value encoding, request its size without alignment, use a 1024-byte stack
buffer through size `0x400`, allocate larger buffers from the default zone,
fill through `getValue:`, and create a typed `NSNumber` in the requested zone.

adaptation. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSString` URL path standardization parity (2026-10-11)

Compared `standardizedURLPath` and `standardizedNativePath` in i386 IDA
(`0x42595dd4`, `0x42596098`) and PPC IDA (`0x425afedc`, `0x425b0308`)

Both targets lazily copy path components only when percent escaping or

decoding likewise preserves the target's PPC conversion-failure path. No
source correction was indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

`0x4262678c`–`0x42626eac`). The other bytes, including the tails beyond IDA's

## `NSAutoreleasePool addObject:` nested-pool insertion parity (2026-10-12)

Compared `-[NSAutoreleasePool addObject:]` in i386 IDA (`0x425732d8`) and PPC

the object through `NSAutoreleaseObject`, get the current thread's pool data,
and return when the pool stack is empty or this pool is already at the top.
For an outer pool, they walk the intervening pool cursors from the top toward
the receiver, move each cursor's next object into the preceding pool's slot,
advance each cursor, allocate a page when its slot reaches the page capacity,
then put the new object in the final insertion slot. The i386 threshold is
expressed as `>= capacity`; PPC uses the equivalent `capacity <= count` form.
Source matches the nested-pool routing, cursor advancement, and page rollover.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteFileHandle` available and length-limited reads (2026-10-12)

Compared `-[NSConcreteFileHandle availableData]` (i386 `0x425792a4`, PPC
`0x4258cc9c`), `readDataOfLength:` (i386 `0x42579af4`, PPC `0x4258d5a0`),
and `readDataToEndOfFile` (i386 `0x42579d5c`, PPC `0x4258d7d4`) with
`NSFileHandle.m`. Both targets reject closed handles and `fstat` failures via
the operation exception helper. `availableData` reads one page for nonregular
files; for regular files it seeks to the current offset and reads the bytes
remaining to the stat size. It returns empty data on a zero-byte read and
otherwise copies only the returned byte count.

For `readDataOfLength:`, both targets use a single read capped by the regular
file's remaining length when the descriptor is regular. Other descriptors use
chunks of at most 4,096 bytes, append the next chunk's capacity after each
successful read, and stop on EOF or when the requested byte count is consumed.
The result contains only the bytes actually read. `readDataToEndOfFile` forwards
`UINT_MAX` (encoded as `-1` in the target call). PPC disassembly confirms the
initial data length and per-iteration `increaseLengthBy:` arguments that
Hex-Rays elides from its call rendering. Source matches both target paths and
ownership behavior. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.

Compared `-[NSConcreteFileHandle initWithFileDescriptor:]` (i386
`0x4257987c`, PPC `0x4258d2a4`),
`initWithFileDescriptor:closeOnDealloc:` (i386 `0x425798a0`, PPC
`0x4258d2dc`), and `initWithPath:flags:createMode:` (i386 `0x425798c0`, PPC
`0x4258d304`) with `NSFileHandle.m`. Both simple descriptor initializers store
the descriptor; the one-argument form forwards `closeOnDealloc:NO`, and the
flag-taking form sets bit 0 only when that argument is false. The path
initializer uses a 4,104-byte stack buffer, asks the default file manager for a
filesystem representation with maximum length 1,024, opens it with the supplied
flags and mode, and stores the returned descriptor on success. Conversion or
open failure invokes the superclass deallocator and returns nil. i386
instruction pushes and PPC register setup confirm the conversion limit and
argument order omitted by pseudocode. Source matches both targets. Static
paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source review only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSMachNMServer` lookup, registration, and copy paths (2026-10-12)

Compared the concrete name-server methods in i386 and PPC IDA with
`NSPortNameServer.m`: `+default` (i386 `0x425445f8`, PPC `0x425483e0`),
`-init` / `-initWithPort:` (i386 `0x42552fe4` / `0x4255300c`, PPC
`0x42555f70` / `0x42555fb0`), `-portForName:onHost:` (i386 `0x4254328c`, PPC
`0x425480dc`), `-portForName:` (i386 `0x42569734`, PPC `0x42575e00`),
`-registerPort:forName:` and `-registerPort:forName:signature:` (i386
`0x42549a0c` / `0x4254812c`, PPC `0x42575e38` / `0x42575ed0`),
`-removePortForName:` and `-removePortForName:signature:` (i386
`0x42569758` / `0x42569784`, PPC `0x42575fd4` / `0x42576010`), plus `count`,
copy, mutable-copy, and deallocation.

Both targets lazily cache the default server without locking, retain the
provided name-server port, and forward one-argument lookup/removal through the
host/signature variants. Lookup converts nil host and name strings to empty C
strings and returns nil when `netname_look_up` fails. Registration lazily
creates the default signature port, checks the service port for `machPort`,
raises the same invalid-argument exception when absent, and returns whether
`netname_check_in` succeeds. i386 evaluates port, signature, then server-port
arguments; PPC evaluates server-port, signature, then port. Removal preserves
the corresponding target order for `netname_check_out`. Both targets report
count zero, copy and mutable-copy as alloc/initialization of the dynamic class,
and release `_nameServerPort` before superclass deallocation. Source matches
these target flows and call-order splits. Static paired IDA/source review only;
no tests or builds were run.

`+[NSMachPort resetAllPorts]`, allocate an NSPort with a nil zone, initialize
it with `name_server_port`, store it in `__NSMachNMServerPort`, and return it.
PPC disassembly confirms the initializer argument that Hex-Rays omits from its
pseudocode. The source matches the full target sequence. Static paired IDA
pseudocode/disassembly and constant decoding only; no tests or builds were
run.

but the exception diagnostic differs. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly
and source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## Abstract `NSString` character access and substring flow (2026-10-12)

`0x4251feb4`) and PPC IDA (`0x425a6da0`, `0x425a7270`, `0x4251dbcc`) with
`NSString.m`. Both targets route `characterAtIndex:` through
`NSRequestConcreteImplementation` and return zero afterward. Range extraction
loops over the requested length and sends `characterAtIndex:` for each offset,
without a separate range check. Substring creation checks both the location and
location-plus-length against `length`, returns the shared empty string for an
empty range, copies a full-range result with the supplied zone, and otherwise
allocates a UTF-16 buffer, fills it through `getCharacters:range:`, and returns
an owning string. The source matches these flows and target bounds diagnostic.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSNotificationCenter` PPC serialized observer removal parity (2026-10-12)

Rechecked the current `NSNotification.m` implementation against i386 and PPC
IDA. i386 `postNotification:` (`0x425284d8`) and
`postNotificationName:object:userInfo:flags:` (`0x42504af8`) snapshot matching
observer records under the optional lock, unlock, then deliver through
`__postNotification` (`0x4251c400`); they expose no serialized-removal flag.
PPC `postNotification:` (`0x4253b8f8`) and
`postNotificationName:object:userInfo:flags:` (`0x4250ac64`) pass the center to
`__postNotification` (`0x425270b0`), which registers a stack record in the
center's circular pending-post list before unlocking. The PPC helper skips
callbacks nulled by same-thread removal, releases a temporary notification,
then reacquires the center lock, unlinks the post record, broadcasts, and
unlocks before re-raising the first callback exception.

PPC `removeObserver:name:object:` (`0x4251cb34`) calls
`_wait_while_posting` (`0x42581508`) when the flag is enabled. Its
`_is_in_posting` helper (`0x425811f8`) nulls matching callbacks from posts on
the current thread and waits only when another thread is still posting to the
observer. The source implements these paths through
`NSNotificationCenterBeginPost`, `NSNotificationCenterIsPostingToObserver`,
`NSNotificationCenterWaitForObserver`, and `NSNotificationCenterEndPost`; its
PPC-only setter is present at `NSNotification.m` and the PPC ABI overlay.
The source's lock, callback, cleanup, and exception order matches the target.
This supersedes the 2026-10-05 coverage note that described these methods as
absent and the posting/removal design as pending. Static paired IDA/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## PPC `NSPrintf` integer conversions (2026-10-12)

digit table and adds `0x` only for nonzero values with `#`; explicit precision

## `_NSZombie` reverse-lookup helper linkage review (2026-10-12)

A cross-file `__private_extern__` helper would not be ABI-neutral under the
current object-surface checker: `macho.py` treats `N_EXT` as external and
`abi_check.py` includes every externally bound definition with a section in
`text_symbols`, without distinguishing `N_PEXT`. The current source's prefix
lookup already matches original class names for zombie classes created by
`_NSDeallocateObject`, which obtains them through `_NSZombieClassForClass`
after it inserts the map entry. Since the absent-map case is outside that
normal path, no helper or source change is needed. Static tool-source and
call-path review only; no tests or builds were run.

pseudocode/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

this implementation for PPC. Static PPC IDA/source review only; no tests or

## `NSLock` core lock-state parity (2026-10-12)

Compared `lock` (i386 `0x42501508`, PPC `0x4251998c`), `unlock` (i386
