`0x425950fc`) with `NSLock.m`. Both targets acquire the internal mutex with
`mutex_try_lock` and fall back to `mutex_wait_lock`. `lock` loops while the
locked byte at offset 24 is set, then sets it and clears the mutex word;
`unlock` clears the byte, signals the condition, and clears the mutex word;
`tryLock` returns whether the byte was clear and sets it only on success.
Source's `mutex_lock` macro expands to the same try/wait sequence, and its
state checks and writes match. The target wait helper uses a `1e20`-second
timeout; the repository cthreads API accepts milliseconds, so source passes
`UINT_MAX` and retries through the same condition loop on timeout. This is the
local API's largest representable wait interval. Static paired IDA/source and
cthreads API review only; no tests or builds were run.

`0x4255c170`, PPC `0x42566258`; `NSConcreteMutableSet` i386 `0x4255ba48`,

`_NSInternalRefCount` for both architectures; that matched i386 but not
the PPC method bodies. Both concrete getters now return the stored count plus
one on PPC and keep the generic internal-count path on i386. Static paired

## `NSFileAttributes fileSize` high-word parity (2026-10-12)

Compared `-[NSFileAttributes fileSize]` in i386 (`0x4253c6b8`) and PPC
(`0x42545764`) IDA with `NSFileManager.m`. Both method encodings declare an
unsigned 64-bit return, but the i386 body loads one word from `self+0x38` and
zeros the high return word; PPC loads one word from `self+0x3c` and zeros the
high return word. `statInfo` begins at `self+8`, and `st_size` begins at byte
48 of the encoded `stat` on both targets, so these loads take its low-order
word under each target's endianness. The source initially returned the full
`statInfo.st_size` value as `unsigned long long`, unlike the target getter's
zero-extended 32-bit result. The getter now converts through `unsigned` before
widening, matching the low word loaded by both targets. The i386 pseudocode's
field label does not agree with the raw load offset, so this conclusion relies
on the machine instructions and runtime type encoding rather than that label.
Static paired IDA disassembly, runtime type-encoding, and source review only;
no tests or builds were run.

## `NSSimpleHashing` counted-dictionary update parity (2026-10-12)

Compared `NSSimpleDictionaryIncrementValue` (i386 `0x425634e4`, PPC
`0x4256db74`) and `NSSimpleDictionaryDecrementValue` (i386 `0x42563364`, PPC
`0x4256d94c`) with `NSSimpleHashing.m`. Increment searches with the masked

returns the stored key and removes the bucket. For the low-capacity table,
removal moves the last bucket into the removed slot before marking the old tail
deleted; larger tables mark the removed slot deleted directly. The source uses
shared lookup and removal helpers for those same branches and preserves the
count and resize behavior on both targets. No source correction indicated.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSSimpleHashing` simple-set insert and delete parity (2026-10-12)

Compared `NSSimpleSetInsert` (i386 `0x4250f240`, PPC `0x4250bef0`) and

`NSSimpleHashing.m`. On an existing value, insertion returns the stored
value and replaces it only when `replaceValue` is true. New entries store the
masked hash and value, saturate the distinct-value count, and resize at the
capacity threshold. Deletion returns the stored value and removes its bucket;
for low-capacity tables it moves the last entry into the removed slot, while
larger tables mark the slot deleted. Source uses the matching lookup, insert,
and removal helpers and preserves these return and mutation paths on both
targets. No source correction indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only;
no tests or builds were run.

## i386 Libc versus PPC Foundation NaN formatting path (2026-10-12)

Compared `src/Libc-1/stdio.subproj/vfprintf.c`, the Foundation call paths, and
PPC IDA `_NSvfprintf` (`0x425121b8`) plus `cvt` (`0x4254f2e0`). The i386
`SubstituteFormat` path calls `vsnprintf`; the in-tree Libc `vfprintf` checks
`isnan` after `isinf` and emits the literal `"NaN"` before entering floating
conversion. PPC Foundation has no NaN short-circuit in `_NSvfprintf`: it calls
`cvt`, whose ordered `value >= 0` test takes the negative-sign branch for an
unordered NaN, then passes the value to `__dtoa`. This is an intentional
architecture-specific formatter path already preserved by `NSMutableString.m`
and `NSPrintf.m`; no source correction is indicated. This comparison records
the dispatch paths and does not assert a complete formatted PPC NaN string for
every conversion. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds
were run.

## PPC `NSPrintf` NaN fixed-format extension boundary (2026-10-12)

Followed the PPC NaN path through `_NSvfprintf` (`0x425121b8`), `cvt`
(`0x4254f2e0`), and `___dtoa` (`0x4254e138`) against `NSPrintf.m` and
`NSDtoa.m`. For NaN, `___dtoa` returns the three-byte `"NaN"` result with
decimal-point position 9999. `cvt` takes the negative-sign path because the
ordered `value >= 0` check is false. For `%f` with its default precision,
`_NSvfprintf` enables alternate form, and `cvt`'s fixed-format trailing-zero
loop extends from the dtoa result to `digits + precision + decpt`. The source
has the same path. This records the target's unusually large write boundary;
it does not establish the memory protection or runtime outcome of that write.
No source correction was indicated. Static paired PPC IDA/source review only;
no tests or builds were run.

## PPC NaN literal storage protection follow-up (2026-10-12)

Resolved the storage-location question left open above. PPC IDA names the
`"NaN"` result `aNan` at `0x42622030` in `__cstring`; that segment has IDA
permissions `READ|EXEC` (`5`) and no `WRITE` permission. The `%f` default-
precision alternate-form path therefore attempts to extend the NaN result
through bytes not represented by that three-byte literal, in a segment IDA
marks non-writable. Static segment permissions do not establish runtime page
protection or the observed failure mode, so the note does not claim a crash.
This confirms a target-side hazard rather than a source/target mismatch; no
product code changed. Static PPC IDA/source review only; no tests or builds
were run.

raise `NSParseErrorException` with the reason, line, position, units, and
next-token values. The i386 pseudocode omits the final variadic argument, but
its call-site disassembly pushes the next-token value before the units array;
the format string in both binaries includes `Next token is '%@'`. PPC passes
the same five values explicitly in the decompilation.

There is a call-order difference: i386 obtains/interns the next-token string
before constructing the units array, while PPC constructs the array first.
`NSParser.m` now preserves both orders with an architecture guard: the i386
branch resolves `nextToken` before `units`, and the PPC branch resolves
`units` before `nextToken`. This closes the source-order gap recorded in the
initial audit. Static paired IDA/source review and diff checking only; no tests
or builds were run.

`NSMutableArray -addObject:` in `NSArray.m`. Both targets check concrete
storage, reject nil, grow capacity by one, retain the object, store the retain
result at the old count, and increment `_info` afterward. Source preserves
that same order. No source correction indicated. Static paired IDA/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSProcessInfo` singleton and globally unique string parity (2026-10-12)

Compared `+[NSProcessInfo processInfo]` (i386 `0x42535d84`, PPC
`0x42527b18`) and `-[NSProcessInfo globallyUniqueString]` (i386 `0x42581558`,
PPC `0x425623a8`) with `NSProcessInfo.m`. Both singleton methods lazily allocate
`NSProcessInfo` in the default zone, initialize it, cache the instance, and
return that cache. Both unique-string methods test `_NSTempFileCounterLock` for nonnil before
sending `lock`/`unlock` to `_NSUniqueStringCounterLock`; the PPC GOT entries
`0x42626e94` and `0x42626e98` resolve to those respective globals. The methods
increment the shared counter, rebuild the prototype after signed overflow
using absolute current time, host name, process ID, and process name, reset the
counter to one, unlock, then append the decimal counter. The target-specific
final format value is preserved: i386 obtains `cString` and supplies its
pointer to the `%d` slot, while PPC supplies the process-name length. Source
matches each target's call sequence and arguments. No source correction
indicated. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

Compared `insertObject:range:` (i386 `0x4251530c`, PPC `0x4253b084`),

old terminal slot, while PPC copies only live following runs; the source keeps

replacement with nil and length zero on both targets. No source correction
indicated. Static paired IDA pseudocode/source review only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `_NSReadMutableAttributedStringWithCoder` dictionary-table growth parity (2026-10-12)

Rechecked the helper at i386 `0x42551c08` and PPC `0x425ab7c8` against
`NSAttributedString.m`. Both decode the backing string, install it through an
empty-range replacement, and return immediately for zero length. For each run,
they decode the integer dictionary ID and run length, cache decoded attribute
dictionaries by ID, and apply the cached dictionary to the run. The temporary
index table starts with 20 zeroed stack slots; an out-of-capacity unsigned ID
grows it to twice the current capacity or `ID + 1`, whichever is larger, and
zeroes the newly added slots. Both decode a dictionary only when its slot is
empty and free a heap-grown table on completion. PPC disassembly confirms an
unsigned `cmplw` for the index/capacity comparison; i386 uses the equivalent
unsigned comparison. Source matches both targets; no correction indicated.
Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source review only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `_NSZombie` original-class lookup fidelity gap (2026-10-12)

Compared `_findOriginalClass` (i386 `0x4257583c`, PPC `0x42586950`) and
`_logMessageAndRaise` (i386 `0x42575890`, PPC `0x42586a58`) with the
`_NSZombie` helper in `NSObject.m`. Both targets enumerate the shared
`classToZombie` map until the zombie class is found as a value, then format the
original class name from the matching key. Source instead strips the
`NSZombie_` prefix from the zombie class name. That yields the same name for
normally synthesized classes, but bypasses the target reverse-map lookup and
differs if a zombie class has no matching map entry. The selector wrappers
and diagnostic format otherwise match. The reverse-lookup helper is absent
from the reference's exported symbol table; adding a cross-file function
would create an ABI divergence recorded in `reconstruction/divergences.md`.
The source retains the prefix lookup. A current call-path check shows
`NSDeallocateObject` obtains each zombie class through
`_NSZombieClassForClass`, which inserts the original-to-zombie mapping before
returning the class assigned to the object's `isa`; therefore the missing-map
case is outside the normal deallocation path. Prefix stripping and the target
reverse lookup yield the same original class name for classes created by that
path. The private helper would add an external object symbol under the current
ABI checker, so no implementation change is warranted for the unreachable
case. Static paired IDA/source and linkage review only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSMachNMServer` copy allocation receiver discrepancy (2026-10-12)

The i386 `copyWithZone:` and `mutableCopyWithZone:` bodies (`0x4256966c`,
`0x425696fc`) load the receiver's first word (`isa`) as the
`allocWithZone:` receiver. PPC does the same (`0x42575d08`, `0x42575dbc`,
`lwz r3, 0(r3)`). Both source methods send `class` to `self` before
allocation. That differs when a subclass overrides `-class`; the IDA-confirmed
correction is to allocate through `(Class)self->isa`. Implementation awaits
the focused design approval. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteFileHandle` read and write body parity (2026-10-12)

Compared `availableData` (i386 `0x425792a4`, PPC `0x4258cc9c`),
`readDataOfLength:` (`0x42579af4`, `0x4258d5a0`),
`readDataToEndOfFile` (`0x42579d5c`, `0x4258d7d4`), and `writeData:`
(`0x4257a0b4`, `0x4258dc98`) with `NSFileHandle.m`. Both targets use the
remaining file size for regular files and `NSPageSize()` for `availableData`
on nonregular descriptors. Length-limited nonregular reads use 4096-byte

## `_NSOpenFileDescriptor` create-mode argument divergence (2026-10-12)

The i386 helper at `0x4254605c` takes path, flags, and mode, then forwards all
three to `open`. PPC IDA decompiles the helper at `0x42555628` with two formal
arguments and renders `open(path, flags)`; its assembly calls `_open` without
setting `r5`. Source now preserves this target-specific call form. On PPC, an
incoming value in `r5` remains untouched across the helper prologue and is
therefore still present at the `_open` call; this is a register pass-through,
not an explicit use of the helper's `mode` parameter. This supersedes the
earlier inference that the source should explicitly pass `mode` on PPC. Static
paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source review only; no tests or builds were
run.

the old one. Exchange swaps concrete storage directly; its generic path
retains the first object, fetches the second, performs two indexed
replacements, then releases the temporary retain. Source preserves these
branches and ownership order on both targets. No correction indicated.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

recorded final-release lock ordering within the full lifecycle. Static paired
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSDecimalNumberPlaceholderForZone` paired helper review (2026-10-13)

Compared the placeholder-for-zone helper in i386 (`0x425a2d78`) and PPC
(`0x4255b0a4`) IDA with `NSDecimalNumber.m`. i386 conditionally uses the
placeholder `NSLock`; PPC acquires its atomic spin lock only when the process is
multithreaded. Both cache by zone, search the placeholder array backward, lazily
create it with capacity 8, allocate a placeholder in the default zone, and
cache it. The source preserves the target-specific lock paths and shared state
flow. No correction indicated. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSUndoRaise` target-specific diagnostic argument order (2026-10-13)

Raw call-site disassembly for `undo` (`0x4256d28c`, `0x4257a0cc`),
`undoNestedGroup` (`0x4256d114`, `0x42579f30`), and `redo`
(`0x4256cd4c`, `0x42579c54`) shows i386 evaluates `NSStringFromClass` before
`NSStringFromSelector`; PPC evaluates the selector first. `NSUndoRaise` now
sequences those calls per target before passing the same three format arguments
to `raise:format:`. This refines the earlier argument-value review, which did
not track evaluation order. Static paired IDA disassembly/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSUndoManager forwardInvocation:` diagnostic call order (2026-10-13)

Raw i386 disassembly of `-[NSUndoManager forwardInvocation:]` (`0x4256ca18`)
evaluates the invocation selector, then the manager class, then `_cmd`'s
selector name before raising. PPC (`0x4254cc14`) evaluates `_cmd`'s selector,
then the manager class, then the invocation selector. The exception values and
message are the same on both targets. `NSUndoManager.m` now sequences these
formatter calls per architecture before the shared raise. Static paired IDA
disassembly/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSUndoInvocation` descriptions call order (2026-10-13)

In `-[_NSUndoInvocation description]`, i386 (`0x4256e548`) evaluates the
invocation selector and converts it before obtaining the target class; PPC
(`0x4257aef8`) obtains the target class before the selector. In
`-[_NSUndoLightInvocation description]`, i386 (`0x4256e62c`) obtains the
argument class when present, converts the stored selector, then obtains the
target class; PPC (`0x4257afc8`) obtains target class, selector, and optional
argument class in that order. `NSUndoManager.m` now sequences these formatter
calls per target while preserving the format arguments. Static paired IDA
disassembly/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `_NSUndoInvocation invoke` dispatch (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`0x4256e608`) and PPC (`0x4257af78`) implement
`-[_NSUndoInvocation invoke]` with a single call:
`[_invocation invokeWithTarget:_target]`. `NSUndoManager.m` previously called
`setTarget:` and then `invoke`; it now uses the target's single dispatch.
Static paired IDA pseudocode/source review and `git diff --check` only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSUndoManager beginUndoGrouping` selector recheck (2026-10-13)

Raw i386 disassembly (`0x42552558`) calls `_prepareEventGrouping` before
choosing the active stack, then conditionally calls
`_postCheckpointNotification` after the groups-by-event/nesting check. PPC
(`0x4254d9a8`) follows the same call flow. The i386 selector reference resolves
to `_prepareEventGrouping`; this corrects the earlier divergence entry that
identified it as `_postCheckpointNotification`. `NSUndoManager.m` now calls
`_prepareEventGrouping` on both targets and preserves the later conditional
checkpoint call. Static paired IDA disassembly/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `_NSUndoStack _removeBottom` pruning flow (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`0x4256e720`) and PPC (`0x4257b0f0`) start at the tail begin mark,
walk toward newer nodes while balancing begin/end marks, release each popped
node, reconnect the remaining tail, and decrement `_count`. The source's
extra empty-list and count guards did not match that flow. Its callers prune
only while `_max` is nonzero and `_count > _max`, so a remaining head is
present after removing the oldest group. `NSUndoManager.m` now follows the
paired loop and updates. Static paired IDA pseudocode/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSHashRemove` null guard order (2026-10-14)

Compared `_NSHashRemove` in i386 IDA (`0x4251a118`) and PPC IDA
(`0x4252a2cc`) with `NSHashTable.m`. Both targets check for a null item and
raise `NSInvalidArgumentException` before reading the table's set or counting
its entries. Source previously loaded `table->set` before the null check; it
now performs that load afterward. Static paired IDA/source review and diff
checking only; no tests or builds were run.

and placeholder construction. IDA confirms their names, starts, and sizes;
each maps to a unique definition in `NSString.m`. The map contains 126
functions. Scoped validation passed schema and source-line checks with zero
unmapped, duplicate, or boundary-disputed entries. No tests or builds were
run.

## PPC NSString source-map boundary correction (2026-10-14)

Adding the NSString C helpers exposed a stale
`-[NSString stringByAppendingFormat:]` mapping at `0x425261e0` with size 123,
which lies inside `__NSNewStringByAppendingStrings`. IDA places the method at
`0x4252669c` with size 176. Corrected the existing mapping to that exact
function range. The strings-text map now validates without overlapping ranges.
No tests or builds were run.

## Architecture-correct Foundation source-map boundaries (2026-10-14)

A boundary audit against the binary identified by each map's
`reference_sha256` found that the four i386 maps (`exceptions-runtime`,
`geometry-range-decimal`, `invocation-coding`, and `object-core`) contained
PPC addresses for recent additions. Corrected 44 function starts/sizes to the
i386 IDA boundaries and removed three names absent from the i386 image:
`__NSExceptionRaiser`, `__NSSetExceptionRaiser`, and
`+[NSInvocation newInvocationWithMethodSignature:]`. The four maps now contain
468 functions, all matching the i386 IDA function boundaries exactly.

The PPC `strings-text` map also contained stale i386 boundaries despite its PPC
reference hash. Replaced 96 entries with PPC IDA starts and ends, retaining the
PPC `__NSNewStringByAppendingStrings` boundary and removing the unmatched
single-underscore alias. All 125 mapped entries now match PPC IDA. The other
44 PPC maps had no boundary discrepancies. Semantic loading of all 49 source
maps passes; the maps contain 3,702 entries total (3,234 PPC and 468 i386).
Static IDA/source-map validation only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSParser nextToken` EOF token-buffer state order (2026-10-13)

Recompared i386 `-[NSParser nextToken]` (`0x4250bf98`) and PPC
(`0x42505504`). Both targets set `_tokenBufferReady` after skipping
whitespace/comments, then return the end token before widening a previously
non-ASCII token buffer or setting `_tokenIsASCII` to true. The source performed
the buffer mutations at method entry and did not set the ready flag until
token processing returned. It now sets the ready flag before classification
and defers widening and the ASCII reset until after the EOF return; count and
input-position resets remain at entry. Static paired IDA pseudocode/source
review and whitespace check only; no tests or builds were run.

## PPC lossy NEXTSTEP-to-ASCII table representation (2026-10-13)

Rechecked `NSUnicodeToLossyASCII` and `lossyNEXTSTEPToASCIITable` in i386
IDA (`0x4259269c`, table symbol `0x425a6de4`) and PPC IDA
(`0x425aa098`, table symbol `0x425ccf80`). i386 extracts each packed word
low byte first. PPC reads the same four-byte record in memory order and emits
its nonzero bytes in sequence. The source initializer values encode those
records as packed little-endian words, so their raw PPC data bytes previously
differed from IDA even though the conversion behavior was equivalent.

The table now byte-swaps each initializer at compile time on PPC, preserving
the IDA record bytes in the big-endian image; i386 initializers remain
unchanged. `NSUnicodeToLossyASCII` reads the four record bytes directly, which
implements the same byte order as i386 extraction and PPC record traversal.
Refreshed source-line anchors in the four maps with entries after the table; two additional maps reference this file only before the edited region. Static
source/IDA-byte reasoning and source-map validation only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `NSConcreteMutableCharacterSet` range and set mutations (2026-10-13)

`formIntersectionWithCharacterSet:` (`0x42588d40`, `0x425a0e80`) with
`NSCharacterSet.m`. Range addition skips zero-length ranges, materializes
mutable bitmap storage as needed, and sets every bit in the inclusive range.
String removal checks mutability, reads the string length once, prepares bitmap
storage, then clears each listed character. Union and intersection prepare
the receiver bitmap, use descending 2,048-word operations for matching
concrete-set instances or other sets that provide a bitmap, and otherwise
query all 65,536 character values. The intersection fallback preserves a bit
only when it was already set and the other set contains that character. Source
matches both targets' branches and operation order; no correction indicated.
Static paired IDA pseudocode/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

`NSCharacterSet.m`. Compact conversion only converts a present bitmap back to

range. The string initializer calls `init`, delegates to

the initialized set storage, stores the supplied set, and returns self. Source
matches both architectures; no correction indicated. Static paired IDA
pseudocode/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSUserDefaults` dictionary representation reconstruction (2026-10-13)

Re-decompiled `computeDictRep` and its call sites in both IDA targets. The
helper returns nil for an empty search list; otherwise it pushes an autorelease
pool, snapshots the list into 128 inline object slots or a zone allocation,
allocates a mutable dictionary with capacity 256 in the passed zone, removes a
trailing registration domain by sending `isEqualToString:` to
`NSRegistrationDomain`, then visits remaining domains in reverse order.
Temporary-domain values take precedence, with defaults-manager values as the
fallback. Both targets pass a null zone at every call site. `NSUserDefaults.m`
now follows this flow, and its i386/PPC source-map anchors after the helper
were shifted to the new source lines. All affected maps pass schema and
semantic validation. No tests or builds were run.

The same `NSArchiver` pass found that `_encodeLong(INT_MIN)` in both binaries
passes an eight-byte range beginning at the address of its four-byte integer
argument. The current source instead sign-extends the value into a local
`long long` before appending eight bytes. Reproducing the binary's range could
copy adjacent stack storage, so this behavior remains under review; no code
change was made for it.

## NSScanner `isAtEnd` skip-set range parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `-[NSScanner isAtEnd]` in i386 IDA (`0x4255299c`, 209 bytes) and PPC IDA (`0x4255ad88`, 224 bytes) with `NSScanner.m:832-845`. Both read the input, current cursor, length, and skip set; when a skip set exists, they invert it and search the remaining input range with options zero. They treat the end as reached when no non-skipped character remains. The i386 disassembly confirms the range is `{scanLocation, length - scanLocation}` despite Hex-Rays omitting those arguments from the call rendering. Source matches both targets. Existing scanner maps anchor the method at line 832. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source-map review only; no tests or builds were run.
## NSUndoManager undo and redo stack transitions (2026-10-15)

Compared `-[NSUndoManager undo]` (i386 `0x4256d28c`, 217 bytes; PPC `0x4257a0cc`, 296 bytes) and `-redo` (i386 `0x4256cd4c`, 399 bytes; PPC `0x42579c54`, 440 bytes) with `NSUndoManager.m:694-756`. `undo` posts a checkpoint, closes the callback-owned group when the undo stack is at nesting level one, clears the callback flag, rejects remaining nested groups, then delegates to `undoNestedGroup`. PPC also cancels the scheduled end-of-event callback after closing that group; i386 has no cancellation call. `redo` gates on `canRedo`, sets the redo flag, validates the top end mark, posts will/did notifications around grouping and invocation, transfers the action name to the undo stack, and clears the flag. The group-identifier transfer is unconditional on i386 and guarded by `_disabled == 0` on PPC. Source preserves both target-specific branches and call order. Existing paired undo-manager maps anchor these functions by name, address, size, and source line. Static paired IDA/source-map review only; no tests or builds were run.

## Lazy deserialization fault dictionary lookup parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `count`, `allKeys`, and `objectForKey:` in i386 IDA (`0x42575fc4`,
41 bytes; `0x42514c18`, 468 bytes; `0x42518e50`, 603 bytes) and PPC IDA
(`0x42587870`, 68 bytes; `0x425876bc`, 436 bytes; `0x42587a50`, 504 bytes)
with `NSSerialization.m:471-552`. Both `count` methods return the handler
count. `allKeys` rejects non-dictionary faults through
`doesNotRecognizeSelector:`, returns the cached key array when present,
otherwise deserializes keys in the receiver's zone, removes nil keys by
replacing them with the last element, builds the array in that zone, releases
temporary keys, frees heap storage above 128 keys, and caches the result.
`objectForKey:` rejects non-dictionary faults, returns nil for an empty or
absent key, lazily creates the key cache, walks serialized key/value-length
records to locate the value table, sums preceding value lengths, and
deserializes the selected value with the handler's mutability, zone, and lazy
threshold. The PPC target uses a block integer-deserialization helper for
preceding value lengths while source loops over the same entries; i386
accumulates them in bounded blocks. The resulting cursor and value arguments
match both targets. Existing paired maps anchor all three methods at their
current declarations. No source correction indicated. Static paired IDA/source-
map review only; no tests or builds were run.
